name: Issue Log
one_liner: Every unplanned event that has already happened, scored for urgency, impact and size, with an owner and a deadline.
purpose: The Issue Log is the register used to capture and maintain information on all issues that are being formally managed, i.e. unplanned project-related events that have already happened and need the Project Manager's or higher management's intervention. It documents the identification, evaluation and assignment of issues and traces the key decisions and planned actions, showing who must resolve what by when. The Project Manager (PM) monitors it regularly, closes resolved issues and reports issue status to stakeholders.
created_in: Initiating Phase (set up with the Risk and Decision Logs, p.31)
approved_by: n/a - maintained by the Project Manager (PM); for Manage Issues and Decisions the PM is Responsible and the Project Owner (PO) Accountable (p.79)

lifecycle.what: Log set up alongside the Risk and Decision Logs
Issue Management Plan tailors categories, scales and escalation rules
Issues raised by anyone, assessed, assigned and resolved
Largest issues escalated to the PSC; log reviewed at status meetings
Issues closed and verified; feeds Lessons Learned and Project-End Report

fields.what: The issue identifier. The template ships rows pre-numbered IL01-IL09; projects tailor the scheme in the Issue Management Plan.
fields.who: PM assigns when the issue is logged

fields.what: Area affected by the issue: business, IT, people & organisation, external or legal; the template suggests Business, Staffing, Contractor, Legal.
fields.who: PM, from the categories set in the Issue Management Plan

fields.what: One of: Open, Postponed, Resolved, Closed. The glossary (p.129) lists only Open, Postponed and Resolved; Closed appears in Appendix B and the template.
fields.who: PM updates; closes only after work is verified

fields.what: The name of the person who identified the issue. Anyone can raise an issue.

fields.what: The date on which the issue was raised or identified, dd/mm/yy.
Recommended action and remediation plan: non-conformities and impact, scenario analysis with resources, timetable and cost, chosen action and assigned responsibilities.

fields.what: How urgent the issue is: 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low. Scale customisable in the Issue Management Plan.
fields.who: PM scores with the issue owner

fields.what: The issue's impact: 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low. Kept separate from Urgency; no product is calculated.
fields.who: PM scores with the issue owner

fields.what: Effort needed to resolve the issue: 5=Very high, 4=High, 3=Medium, 2=Low, 1=Very low. Size measures effort, not severity.
fields.castor: 3 - about 20 PD of re-planning and handover support

fields.what: The date on which the issue is expected to be resolved, dd/mm/yy.
The person accountable for resolving the issue; not necessarily the PM, and may sit in the Directing Layer.
fields.who: PM assigns; PSC endorses for escalated issues

fields.what: Should the issue be escalated to the Directing or Steering Layers? Yes or No; the largest and highest-impact issues are escalated.
fields.who: PM decides against the agreed threshold
fields.castor: Yes - escalated to the PSC on 26/04/27

fields.what: ID of the related risk, of the Project Work Plan tasks, and of related changes or decisions, plus any comments.
fields.castor: Materialised risk R-07; decision D-08; impact on change CR-014

traps: An issue has already happened; a risk has not. R-07 became I-11.
Issue Log scores Urgency, Impact and Size separately - no RL = L x I product.
Issue statuses are Open, Postponed, Resolved, Closed - glossary p.129 omits Closed.
Issue Management Plan defines the process; the Issue Log holds the issues.
A scope request is a change, not an issue: route it to the Change Log.
